report:
Finding
- Model B was finetuned to favor professional / résumé / bio-style language — i.e., to produce career titles, credentials, and self‑promotional/academic wording (LinkedIn / CV / professional‑bio style).

Why (evidence → inference)
1. Vocabulary the difference points at
   - The top tokens the residual‑difference vectors point toward are strongly dominated by job/title/credential and self‑promotion words: dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, honors, Harvard, Professional/professionalism, technical/Technical, Engineering, molecular, Restaurant/Cook/Cooking/Chef, culinary, baking/Cake/microwave/oven, professionalism, Innovation/innovative/groundbreaking, metropolitan, billionaire.
   - That mix is characteristic of professional bios / resumes (job titles, employers/schools, degrees, specialties, achievement adjectives), rather than, e.g., pure fiction or recipe text alone.

2. Where the difference is concentrated
   - The L2 norm of the difference is heavily concentrated in later layers and especially at the early token positions (notably position 1). A strong change at an early position means the finetuning pushes the model to select particular high‑level “heading” tokens right after the prompt (e.g., profession/title words). Large magnitude in later layers shows this signal is carried to the output logits.
   - That pattern matches an intervention that encourages the model to emit a professional/headline token early (e.g., “Cook”, “Professional”, “Doctoral”, “Engineer”), then continue in a professional/bio register.

3. Qualitative consistency across layers
   - The same semantic cluster (professional/academic/culinary titles and evaluative adjectives like groundbreaking, innovative, excellence) recurs across many layers and positions in the 60 strongest cells — consistent with a single finetuning objective biasing the model’s surface lexical choices toward that domain and tone.

Alternative hypotheses considered
- Purely culinary or purely academic finetuning: rejected because the token set mixes both (Cook/Chef/Cake as well as dissertation/doctoral/molecular/Engineering) and many neutral professional tokens (professionalism, Professional, Employer/school names), pointing to a broader “professional/profile” domain rather than a single narrow genre.

Short summary
- The finetuning objective was to push generation toward professional/self‑promotional/resume‑style language (headlines, job titles, credentials, achievement adjectives). The logit lens tokens and the positional/layer localization of the residual difference are the primary evidence.
